mappings.note: All three guesses about the chest, gathered from the text. Rejected LO-8: a set of located details, not the tale's usefulness.
Which particular statements convinced the king -- the learner must collect the specific points. Rejected LO-6: no idea is being weighed.
What the king told the camel's owner and why -- both stated in the text. Rejected LO-6: reported, not appraised.
Why the king held them innocent -- the reasons are narrated. Rejected LO-8: not the moral of the tale.
What sets the brothers apart from ordinary people -- a judgement about the whole tale and the quality it holds up. Rejected LO-9: no single point answers it.

The lesson of 'Teen Buddhimaan' -- the text's usefulness read off the whole. Rejected LO-10: this is a translated tale in a reader, not folk material from the learner's own surroundings, which is what that outcome names.
The footprint evidence for the woman and child. Rejected LO-8: specific evidence, not gist.
All three camel inferences with their grounds -- close examination of the passage. Rejected LO-6: no appraisal invited.
Which wealth the father named. Rejected LO-6, which I keep for the version of this item that also demands the justification.

Meaning of the figurative phrase 'doosre prakaar ka dhan', which the key unpacks as a metaphor that grows when shared -- fine grain of language. Rejected LO-9: the difficulty is the figure, not a locatable fact.
How the test was set and how each brother met it -- a chain of located details. Rejected LO-8: procedure, not purpose.
The honour given, and then explicitly the MESSAGE the ending carries -- the text's usefulness. Rejected LO-9: the second half has no locatable answer.
Asks for a detailed account of each inference and its evidence. Rejected LO-8: the demand is for the specifics, not the point.

Which wealth, WHY, and how the sons bore the teaching out -- grasping the author's proposition about wealth and tracing it through the narrative. Rejected LO-9, used where only the name of the wealth is wanted.
How honesty and intelligence won them respect -- the tale's governing claim. Rejected LO-9: no single detail carries it.
'Is it possible to infer correctly without seeing? Express your view' -- the learner must take a position on the text's central claim. Rejected LO-8: a personal stance, not a statement of usefulness.
What their keen observation teaches US -- the text's use, extended to daily life by the key. Rejected LO-9: not a located point.

'If you were the king, how would you honour them' -- a composition in the learner's own voice, which is what this outcome covers. Rejected LO-6: nothing in the author's idea is being agreed with or disputed, only imagined differently.

Why the chest was sent for AND which trait of the king it reveals -- the second half requires reading the author's characterisation. Rejected LO-9, which fits the bare 'why the chest' item but not the inference about the king.
Which wealth the father urged, answered from the printed extract. Rejected LO-12: the phrase is quoted in the extract, not glossed.
What the brothers decided after the death, from the extract. Rejected LO-8: located detail.
Number of days walked, from the extract. Rejected LO-8: bare figure.
What the father valued above property -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-6: no justification demanded here.
WHY intelligence is called 'such wealth' -- the learner must restate the father's reasoning that it never runs out. Rejected LO-9: the reason is argued, not simply found.
The eldest brother's inference from the road, from the extract. Rejected LO-8: specific point.
The middle brother's distinctive observation. Rejected LO-8: detail.
Who was riding the camel, from the extract. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
Which brother looked first and what he inferred -- two located points. Rejected LO-6: no evaluation.
The observation AND its basis (grass cropped on one side) -- close examination. Rejected LO-8: evidence, not usefulness.
What the king asked them to do, from the extract. Rejected LO-8: located instruction.
What the middle brother said was in the chest. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
What the youngest added about the chest's contents. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
Who objected to being called thieves -- attribution within the extract. Rejected LO-6: no appraisal of the objection.
What the brothers were watching from a distance -- the extract states it exactly. Rejected LO-8: located detail.
Which quality astonished the king, from the extract. Rejected LO-12: the phrase is quoted, not defined.
Who said the garden's pomegranates were unripe. Rejected LO-8: attribution detail.
The honour the king finally gave. Rejected LO-8, which I use for the item that also asks for the message.
What the king saw in his garden. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
What the king saw through the open window. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
Which wealth the poor man named, from the extract. Rejected LO-12: the phrase is quoted.
What the poor man kept telling his sons ('understand every thing and situation') -- stated in the extract. Rejected LO-6: reported instruction, not a proposition to weigh.
Completes the father's stated promise about becoming wise. Rejected LO-6: the reasoning is not asked, only the clause.
Which kind of intelligence and sight the man spoke of. Rejected LO-12: quoted, not glossed.
What the sons did after the death and why -- both in the extract. Rejected LO-14: it is the characters' decision, not the learner's own writing.
Whose ear the king whispered into. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
Who the minister returned with. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
What was in the chest. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
The king's reaction on opening the chest -- the extract states his astonishment. Rejected LO-6: given, not inferred.
Where the chest was placed and why -- both located. Rejected LO-6: the king's motive is stated.
What prompted the king's instruction to the camel's owner. Rejected LO-8: a located cause.
How the king received them (by feeding them) -- detail from the extract. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
How the eldest knew the camel was large -- the dust prints. Rejected LO-6: evidence, not idea.
What the king did after opening the chest. Rejected LO-8: sequence detail.
What the brothers PROVED at court -- a summary judgement about the whole episode and what it demonstrates. Rejected LO-9: no single detail states it.
